sections.body: A SCALE is a set of notes in order, going up or down. The C major scale uses only the white keys on a piano: C D E F G A B C.
MELODY is a sequence of single notes, the part you can hum. HARMONY is notes played at the same time to support the melody.
A CHORD is three or more notes played together. The most common is a triad: the 1st, 3rd and 5th notes of a scale.
C major chord = C, E and G (notes 1, 3 and 5 of the C major scale). Major chords often sound bright; minor chords often sound sadder.
Many popular songs use just four chords, repeated in different patterns.
On a free online piano, play C–E–G together, then A–C–E (A minor). How does each sound?

quiz.q: Which notes make a C major chord?
hints: A triad uses notes 1, 3 and 5 of the scale.
C major scale: C(1) D(2) E(3) F(4) G(5)…
G major scale: G A B C D… Notes 1, 3, 5 are G, B, D. Use the same pattern for C.
quiz.explain: Notes 1, 3 and 5 of the C major scale are C, E and G.

quiz.q: Playing three or more notes at the same time makes a…
hints: Is it notes in order, or at the same time?
A scale is notes one after another.
A melody is one note at a time, like singing. Notes together are a…?
quiz.explain: Three or more notes played together make a chord.

quiz.q: The part of a song you can hum is the…
hints: Humming is one note at a time.
When you whistle a tune, you're whistling its…?
quiz.explain: The melody is the tune: single notes you can hum or sing.
